official.description: Funded by a gift from the Lee Foundation, the Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme is one of SMU's most prestigious undergraduate scholarships, offering high-calibre individuals holistic, intellectual and entrepreneurial development with up to 60 scholarships funded. Scholars receive a full four-year tuition fee waiver, a S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant, a S$5,000 annual living allowance and a S$1,800 one-time computer allowance, plus development programmes run by SMU's Student Success Centre. It is bond-free, but non-Singaporean scholars must sign an MOE Tuition Grant agreement carrying a 3-year obligation to work for Singapore-based companies.
official.program_type: Distinguished donor-funded merit scholarship for first-year SMU undergraduates, administered by SMU's Office of Admissions & Financial Assistance
official.english_requirement: SMU requires a standardised test score (any one of SAT, ACT, IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, C1 Advanced, PTE Academic or Aptitude Scholastic Test) for applicants under the International and Other Qualifications category. Minimums for non-law programmes: IELTS (Academic) overall 7.0 with at least 7.0 reading and 6.5 writing; TOEFL iBT minimum 93 with 22 reading and 22 writing for tests taken before 21 January 2026, or minimum 5 with 5 reading and 4.5 writing from 21 January 2026; PTE Academic overall 66 with 66 reading and 56 writing. For the Law programme the minimum is IELTS (Academic) overall 7.5 with 7.0 reading and 7.0 writing. Scores are valid for 2 years and the test is not required for IB Diploma holders or acceptable LASALLE, NAFA and NIE diplomas.

applicant_utility.summary: This is SMU's flagship freshman scholarship and it is applied for through the ordinary admission form, so the scholarship decision and the admission decision are made from the same file. Build the application around the second-major requirement rather than treating it as an afterthought: scholars in Business Management must take a second major from a different SMU School, while scholars in Accountancy, Economics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Computing & Law, Software Engineering, Social Sciences or Law must take their second major from the Lee Kong Chian School of Business. Because only up to 60 awards are made and shortlisting is explicitly on academic qualifications plus non-academic records, your essay and referee letter need to evidence leadership and a sustained community-service record, not a list of one-off events. Start early: the personal essay, the referee nomination and the standardised test score all sit inside the same window as the admission application, and predicted scores attested by a school teacher or counsellor are accepted if your final results are not out yet.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving school leavers of any nationality who want a business-adjacent or interdisciplinary SMU degree, will commit to a second major or double degree, and already have a leadership and community-service track record to point at.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm which SMU qualification category you fall under and check that your high school qualification appears on SMU's list of accepted international qualifications
Book SAT, ACT, IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, C1 Advanced, PTE Academic or AST early enough to sit before the closing date, remembering scores are only valid for 2 years
Have your school teacher or counsellor attest predicted scores if your final results will not be released before the deadline - self-declared predictions are not accepted
Draft the scholarship personal essay before the admission form opens, so the essay never becomes the reason you submit late
Warn your tutor or principal before you nominate them as referee, since the recommendation is submitted online and you cannot control their timing
Decide in advance which second major or double degree route you will take, and be ready to write about it in the essay and interview
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the admission application without ever completing the Scholarship section, which silently removes you from consideration because there is no separate scholarship form
A thin or generic personal essay that lists positions held instead of showing leadership, communication and a sustained service commitment
A co-curricular record built from one-off events rather than a substantial, sustained record of involvement
A referee who never submits the recommendation because they were nominated too late
Missing the standardised test score or uploading a score that has expired or was assembled from different sittings - SMU does not accept combined section scores
Not understanding that the second major is a condition of holding the award, not a preference, so scholars who cannot commit to it are not viable
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award waives subsidised tuition for regular terms and pays a S$5,000 annual living allowance, so you still fund accommodation, meals, transport, the student pass and airfare, plus anything the Global Opportunities grant does not cover on an overseas programme. SMU also charges a non-refundable S$15 admission application fee, and you bear the full cost of any standardised test you sit.

You must both upload a copy of your test score and have the testing agency send the official score electronically to SMU (TOEFL destination code 9014, SAT 2861, ACT 5284; for IELTS and C1 Advanced select Singapore Management University from the drop-down list)

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate fellowship form to fill in - you apply to the SUTD PhD Programme and the President's Graduate Fellowship is conferred on admitted awardees, so the strength of your research fit is what actually decides the funding. Your single most important input is the Statement of Objectives plus the faculty you name, because SUTD requires applicants to indicate research topics of interest and lets you identify faculty whose focus aligns with yours. Put real time into the three academic referees, who must each submit their online recommendation within one week of your submission - a slow referee stalls your whole application. If your undergraduate degree was not taught in English, plan for IELTS or TOEFL scores to follow up to two weeks after the closing date, and pay the S$21.80 fee by the deadline or the application will not be processed at all.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Research-led applicants with a strong bachelor's or master's record who want full tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend and can identify a SUTD supervisor whose work actually overlaps with their own.
application_readiness_checklist: Read SUTD's faculty research areas and name one or more potential supervisors in the application whose work genuinely matches your Statement of Objectives
Line up three academic referees early and get their explicit agreement, since each must submit online within a week of your submission
Draft and trim the Statement of Objectives to 3,000 words, and have it reviewed before you open the portal
Assemble full degree certificates and transcripts including the grading policy, plus certified English translations for any non-English document
Sit IELTS or TOEFL early if your degree was not taught in English - the minimum is 6.5 IELTS or 90 TOEFL iBT, and scores can land up to two weeks after the deadline
Consider sitting the GRE even though it is optional, since SUTD calls it highly recommended
Pay the S$21.80 application fee inside the portal before the closing date so the application is processed
common_rejection_risks: A Statement of Objectives or supervisor choice that does not match any active SUTD research group, leaving no faculty member willing to support the application
Referees who fail to submit their recommendations inside the one-week window
Incomplete transcripts or a missing grading policy, which makes it impossible for the panel to read your academic standing
Failing to pay the application fee by the closing date, which stops the application being processed regardless of its merits
Overlooking the teaching and laboratory supervision duties that are a condition of the subsidised fees
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The Fellowship covers applicable tuition fees for up to four years and pays a monthly stipend, but publishes no travel, installation, book, computer or thesis allowance, so flights to Singapore, accommodation, insurance and research expenses are yours to fund. You also pay the S$21.80 application fee, the cost of any English test or GRE you sit, and any translation fees for non-English documents.
document_audit: Every uploaded document must be in English or accompanied by a certified English translation, and translations are at your own expense

If you have not yet graduated you need an official letter of certification from your institution stating the expected date of graduation or award of degree - a predicted grade alone is not the document
Transcripts must include the grading policy or system, not just the marks
If you hold a master's degree you must submit both the certificate and the official transcripts, not only the bachelor's record
Referee recommendations are submitted by the referees themselves online, so confirm institutional email addresses rather than personal ones

There are two PhD intakes a year, in January and September, so a missed January window is not fatal but pushes you back a full cycle
The stipend is citizenship-tiered: S$4,300 for international students versus S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, and only Singapore Citizens receive CPF contributions on top
